I've given this a lot of thought, and before you immediately jump the "omg, privacy!" train, hear me out.

As a little background to supercookies, I'll explain what they are. A cookie is a piece of data that is logged to your machine (roughly speaking) that can store settings and can be used to enhance the experience of a site. Generally used for such things as auto login, etc. A super-cookie, is one that uses a bunch of methods of storing these cookies - through flash storage methods, browser identification (unique addons can be used to positively and uniquely identify your computer) and through the use of these multiple methods can keep itself present in a system through typical wiping processes such as clearing your cookies or erasing your history.

The immediate thought process is "omg, they're tracking me!" and most people immediately jump on the train to backlash city, citing privacy reasons, etc.

But in Voat or even Reddit's case you specifically come to the site because this kind of tracking is happening. Your every interest is tracked through your username and your subverse subscriptions, you rely on other people being tracked and their comments being the proof that they are a single individual with a mind of their own. You rely on proper tracking of upvoats and downvoats to generate the articles that you read. Everything you do on this site is 100%, automatically tracked, even your IP address and the "Verifying your bits" already exist to try and ensure that you are a legitimate user. Every user already relies on this tracking, and this tracking being the same for everyone else in order for this site to function.

I believe that if Voat.co implemented this more heavy-handed version of tracking, and even resorted to the unique identifiers that a lot of mobile operators are injecting into HTTP headers, that Voat.co would better be able to ensure that account-hoppers, paid shills, and brigaders are less able to influence and dictate the things that appear on the site. Additionally, I believe that internally having an API key that an account used that was derived from this account flag would allow voat to still be used by external programs (mobile apps and the like) and keep this information without hamstringing the ability to use voat elsewhere.

In addition, it can actually be used to solve other technical problems such as IP-range banning, where a voat user shares his/her IP address with someone else behind a corporate firewall or something similar. Users can be tracked per-browser, so that a brigader or account hopper on one computer behind an IP address can be separately identified from an innocent party that simply shares the same IP address.

While this is somewhat of a heavy handed approach, but I believe it would make Voat a place that is truly run by the people who visit it and had a little protection against the easily-gamed reddit style platform.
